component.name: Wave Terminal
component.summary: Terminal with inline graphics, file previews and remote connections

description.p: This is a community package of Wave Terminal, maintained independently and unaffiliated with the Wave Terminal project. It repackages the official upstream .deb unmodified and follows upstream releases automatically.

Wave is a terminal that lays out its window as a grid of blocks. A block can be a shell session, but it can just as easily be a file preview, a directory listing, a web view, a CPU graph or an AI chat — all in the same tab, all scriptable from the command line through the bundled wsh helper.

ul.li: Tabbed, tiled terminal blocks with persistent sessions and workspaces.
Remote connections over SSH, reading your existing SSH config, with the same block layout applied to the remote machine.
Inline previews for files, images, Markdown and CSV, plus a directory browser and an editor.
An embedded web block and system-monitor graphs alongside the shell.
AI chat blocks against your own provider key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter and compatible endpoints).

description.p: Permissions: this package grants network access (SSH and the AI providers), the GPU, notifications and the Secret Service for stored connection secrets. It grants no filesystem access — file open and save go through the portal, and Wave's own data stays inside the sandbox. A few capabilities are not granted by default; enable the ones you need with flatpak override:

ul.li: Reuse your existing host SSH keys and config: flatpak override --user --filesystem=~/.ssh:ro dev.commandline.waveterm
Browse and preview files across your home directory: flatpak override --user --filesystem=home dev.commandline.waveterm

description.p: Updates and telemetry: the in-app updater is switched off on first run, because Flatpak installs are updated by Flatpak — re-enable it in Settings if you want the check back. Wave's usage telemetry is left at upstream's default (on) and is a switch in the same Settings panel.

Scope: the built-in local terminal runs inside the sandbox, on the shells the Flatpak runtime provides — not on your host system. Remote (SSH) connections are unaffected and behave exactly as they do elsewhere. Wave's Tsunami widget builder compiles Go on the fly and so needs a Go toolchain, which is not part of this package; the rest of the app does not.
